text.p: Bonds soared on the back of mounting optimism that both Spain and Portugal will get the green light to join monetary union (EMU) at its launch in 1999, traders said.

They said they expected the longer end of the yield curve to track Spain on Wednesday, with the spread between the two 10-year cash markets holding at 15 basis points after narrowing from 25 at Monday's close.
Something of a supply squeeze underpinned the advance, they added. "Futures and the 10-year cash closed very strong and without any signs of a correction tomorrow," said one trader.
The market ended Tuesday close to record highs.
Traders said that expressions of optimism by French President Jacques Chirac about Spain's chances of making the cut for EMU further galvanised both Iberian markets.
"The lack of paper in the 10-year is supporting the rise," added another trader. "Tomorrow, we should see yields at a record low," he said.
Supply is being kept tight by the Treasury's drip-feeding of new paper. The Treasury only accepted bids for 10 billion escudos at today's 10-year auction.
